ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Urinary and gastrointestinal effects

A 67-year-old man develops dry mouth, blurred near vision and difficulty initiating urination a week after starting imipramine. He also reports constipation. His prostate had previously caused mild urinary symptoms. Which receptor action best unifies these new adverse effects?

  1. Beta-2 receptor agonism
  2. Alpha-2 receptor agonism
  3. Muscarinic receptor antagonism
  4. Dopamine D2 receptor antagonism
  5. Histamine H1 receptor antagonism
Answer and explanation

Muscarinic receptor antagonism

Reduced parasympathetic signaling affects salivation, accommodation, bladder emptying and bowel motility.

Option explanations

Muscarinic receptor antagonism: Reduced parasympathetic signaling affects salivation, accommodation, bladder emptying and bowel motility.

Dopamine D2 receptor antagonism: This would more characteristically cause extrapyramidal effects or hyperprolactinemia.

Histamine H1 receptor antagonism: H1 blockade explains sedation better than this autonomic cluster.

Beta-2 receptor agonism: This does not explain reduced secretions and impaired accommodation.

Alpha-2 receptor agonism: This is not the key action producing the described tricyclic anticholinergic effects.
